title: Headphone mix independent of the fader
text: For a performer’s headphone mix, use a pre-fader auxiliary send. Changing the main channel fader then leaves the cue level alone. Verify which mute and insert stages still affect that send.

title: Echo only during software monitoring
text: A delayed double while recording often means direct monitoring and the DAW return are both audible. Listen to one path at a time. For the DAW path, a smaller buffer can reduce monitoring latency.

title: Two microphones lose bass when combined
text: Audition the microphones individually, then sum them to mono. Compare polarity and arrival time. Reversing polarity can help some frequency bands; moving one microphone changes the time difference.

title: Clicks on a digital audio link
text: On a digital link, set both devices to the same sample rate and select one clock master. Confirm the receiver reports clock lock. A clock mismatch can cause intermittent clicks even below clipping level.

title: Mono compatibility of a stereo mix
text: Check the stereo bus in mono. Wide decorrelated effects can cancel during summing. Compare the dry centre with the widened return before reducing stereo width.

title: Clipping before the channel fader
text: If the input converter clips, lowering the DAW fader only makes the distorted recording quieter. Reduce input gain and record a new take. Leave peak headroom for the loudest passage.

title: Parallel reverb return level
text: On a reverb return shared by sends, set the effect wet-only to avoid duplicating the dry signal. Balance the amount with each send and the return fader.

title: Time-based effects and song tempo
text: A quarter note lasts 60000 divided by BPM milliseconds. Multiply by 1.5 for a dotted quarter. Listen to the repeats against the groove before printing them.

title: Writing fader moves over existing automation
text: Use read mode to play existing automation. Touch writes while the control is held and then returns to the previous lane. Check the automation mode before another playback pass.

title: Exporting tails after the final region
text: Extend the render range beyond the final audio region until the reverb and delay decay. Check the exported file's ending rather than only the timeline preview.

title: Matching gain for an effect comparison
text: Match perceived output loudness between processed and bypassed versions. Switch between them on the same passage. A louder output can bias the comparison.

title: Collecting referenced media for transfer
text: Collect external audio into the session folder and include it in the transfer. Open the copy from a different location and verify playback before archiving.
